description: FIRST golden set (kept as evidence, not the one the report uses): five queries that paraphrase the summary of one budget each. Measured on 2026-11-09, every configuration scored precision@5 = 1.00 on four of the five queries and the vector baseline 1.00 on all five: with 15 budgets and the parent-project header in every chunk, a paraphrase of a budget's own summary is found by the embedding alone, so this set cannot tell the configurations apart. golden_set.json replaces it with client briefs that have no one-to-one budget. Relevance is binary at budget level, annotated by hand before running anything.
annotation_notes: Queries are written in English, the language of the corpus. The project's real inputs are Spanish transcripts; session 09 showed that language mismatch alone costs ~0.09 of cosine distance, and query reformulation is out of scope for this exercise, so the golden set isolates the retrieval question from the language question.

Annotation was done before running any configuration, reading the fifteen budgets component by component. Strict criterion: a budget is relevant when an estimator would open it as a reference for most of the project's components, not when it merely shares the sector.

Queries were written with natural domain vocabulary; some of it happens to match component names exactly (OEE, proof of delivery, credit scoring, reminders, returns), which is what gives the lexical branch something to contribute.

queries.query: Online store for a fashion brand: product catalogue with sizes and colours, search with filters, shopping cart, card payments at checkout and order management with returns.
queries.rationale: BUD-2024-021 is the same project (headless fashion storefront: catalog, search, cart + Stripe, storefront, orders and returns). BUD-2022-004 (mobile shopping app with in-app payments and pickup) and BUD-2025-008 (online bakery shop on WooCommerce with subscriptions) are B2C shops whose catalog, checkout and payment components are direct references.

distractors.BUD-2025-003: Payment gateway (card tokenisation, 3-D Secure, acquirer routing). Shares 'card payments' and 'checkout' vocabulary; it is PCI infrastructure, useless to estimate a shop. The exact confusion the exercise describes.
distractors.BUD-2023-012: B2B marketplace (vendor onboarding, tiered pricing, quotes, SAP). Same sector label, different business model; only catalog upload and shipping overlap.

queries.query: Web portal for a chain of physiotherapy clinics: patients book appointments online, receive reminders before the visit and log in to see their visit history, invoices and treatment plans.
queries.rationale: BUD-2024-002 is the same project for dental clinics (booking engine, SMS/WhatsApp reminders, patient portal, clinical records sync). BUD-2023-016 (telemedicine) covers physician scheduling and booking, patient-facing records and consent: a valid reference for the booking and records parts even though video consultations are not asked for.

distractors.BUD-2025-011: Laboratory results portal. Same sector and the word 'portal', but the project is HL7/ASTM analyser integration and result validation; only its patient portal component is comparable.

queries.query: Delivery management platform for a courier company: daily route planning for the fleet, a mobile app for drivers with proof of delivery, and a tracking page where customers follow their parcel.
queries.rationale: BUD-2024-009 (last-mile delivery: route optimisation, driver app with proof of delivery, customer tracking, shipper portal, invoicing) is the only logistics budget and matches component by component.

distractors.BUD-2025-017: Warehouse and inventory management with barcode scanning: logistics-adjacent vocabulary (shipping, picking), different problem.
distractors.BUD-2023-025: IoT predictive maintenance with a 'fleet dashboard' of refrigeration units: shares 'fleet' and 'alerts', nothing to do with deliveries.
distractors.BUD-2022-004: Mobile shopping app with store pickup: shares 'mobile app' and 'pickup', it is retail.

queries.query: Consumer lending platform: online loan application with identity verification, automated credit scoring, electronic signature of the contract and a back office for analysts to review applications.
queries.rationale: BUD-2023-007 (loan origination: KYC onboarding, credit scoring engine, contract e-signature, disbursement, back-office portal) is the same project.

distractors.BUD-2024-014: Mobile banking API (OAuth, PSD2 connectors, accounts). Same sector, different product.
distractors.BUD-2022-019: Robo-advisor: the MiFID suitability questionnaire resembles 'onboarding', the rest is portfolio management.
distractors.BUD-2025-003: Payment gateway: finance vocabulary, unrelated to lending.
distractors.BUD-2023-016: Telemedicine: 'digital signature by the physician' is a lexical trap for 'electronic signature'.

queries.query: Plant monitoring system for a food factory: capture machine and sensor data from the shop floor, compute OEE per line and shift, and alert the maintenance team when a machine shows anomalies.
queries.rationale: BUD-2024-030 (MES for a steel plant: shop-floor data acquisition, OEE and downtime dashboards, maintenance requests) matches the monitoring and OEE parts; BUD-2023-025 (IoT telemetry ingestion, anomaly detection and alerting with technician dispatch) matches the sensor and alerting parts. An estimator would use both.

distractors.BUD-2025-017: Warehouse management for a packaging manufacturer: same 'industrial' sector label, nothing about machines, OEE or sensors.
distractors.BUD-2024-009: Last-mile delivery: shares 'alerts/notifications' and 'live tracking' vocabulary.
